mechanism: BTC is the most liquid, most informationally-efficient instrument on the venue: whales, arbitrageurs and cross-venue basis traders express new information there first (tightest spreads, deepest book). Thinner alt order books absorb the same macro/flow information with a measurable lag because slower, less-informed retail flow dominates alt liquidity provision. When BTC has already moved but a given alt has not yet caught up proportionally, the alt is expected to continue drifting toward BTC's direction as the lag closes.
counterparty: Retail/passive alt holders and market makers on the thinner side of low-cap alt order books (1000PEPE, 1000SHIB, ONDO, TAO, GIGGLE, NEAR, SUI, DOGE, XRP) who have not yet repriced on the same information BTC's deeper, more liquid book already absorbed; they are the forced counterparty because their resting quotes are stale relative to the information already public in BTC's price, and they pay the spread/adverse-selection cost to whoever trades the lag.
prediction: On 1h closed bars of the long_1h dataset (train era), when BTC's trailing 3-bar return exceeds +/-150bps AND the alt's own trailing 3-bar return has NOT yet moved more than 60bps in that same direction, the alt's next-bars return (up to a 6-bar/6h hold) is directionally biased toward BTC's move, net of the 11.5bps round-trip cost, with observed win rate >= p*(150bps) = 53.83% (fee_math.p_star(150)) and bootstrap CI95 of net bps excluding zero. Falsified if the observed net-bps CI on train data spans zero or the mean sits at/below 0.

nearest_dead_rows.why_different: Row 2 (short-horizon alt-vs-ETH reversion, high-vol) bets on MEAN REVERSION of the alt back toward ETH after a divergence; this thesis bets on CONTINUATION/catch-up in BTC's direction while the alt has NOT yet moved -- the opposite directional bet, and it uses BTC (not ETH) as the reference with an explicit lag-not-yet-closed filter row 2 never had.

Row 5 (cross-sectional momentum) is a ranked, ~100-470-name relative-value basket that requires a large cross-section and dies at 1-3 positions; this thesis is a single-symbol, single-reference-asset (BTC) time-series signal screened one alt at a time, never ranks or nets long/short legs across a basket, and needs no cross-sectional breadth to function.

Row 16 (cross-venue funding arb) is a delta-neutral carry trade between two DIFFERENT exchanges' funding rates and dies on geoblocking/track-record grounds; this thesis is a single-venue (Phemex-only, matching desk data access) directional lead-lag momentum trade with no funding-carry leg and no cross-exchange execution requirement.

evidence: (1) Asia-Pacific Financial Markets, 'Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy' (2026, springer link above): using high-frequency data the paper reports small-cap cryptocurrencies show significant delayed responses to BTC price movements, Granger causality tests show a UNIDIRECTIONAL causal relationship from BTC to altcoins (not the reverse), and a lag-trading strategy using BTC's preceding returns as a leading indicator is reported to consistently outperform buy-and-hold across market conditions -- directly supports the lag-then-catch-up mechanism this thesis screens for. (2) arXiv:2606.25466 'Time-dependent weighted directed networks of cryptocurrency interaction from high-frequency returns' (2606 = 2026 pre-print numbering): reports BTC(XBT)->ETH Granger causality at 1-minute return frequency with an optimal lag of 2 minutes, variance reduction 3.24%, F-statistic 171.4 (p<1e-10) -- confirms BTC leads even the second-most-liquid asset at short lags, and that reverse (alt->BTC) causality mostly fails to reject the null, i.e. the direction this thesis trades (BTC->alt, not alt->BTC) matches the documented asymmetry. (3) dergipark.org.tr 'bitcoin's lagged effect on altcoins: a short-term research' -- an open-access short-term empirical study of BTC's lagged transmission into altcoin prices, corroborating a short-horizon (sub-daily) delayed-response structure consistent with the 1h/6-bar hold window used here. None of the three sources report win-rate or bps statistics usable directly for fee_math -- p* and the net-bps CI are computed from this desk's own train-data screen only, per STANDARDS #8.

spec.doa_line: Kill if, on train-era long_1h data (n>=30), the bootstrap CI95 of net bps (fee_math.C_BPS=11.5 already netted) includes zero, OR observed win rate < fee_math.p_star(150)=0.5383, OR either +/-20% tp_bps robustness variant flips net_bps_mean sign relative to the base case.

signal_py:
"""informed_flow_btc_lead_alt -- BTC leads illiquid altcoins on the same venue (Phemex,
long_1h dataset, 1h bars). Mechanism: BTC is the venue's most liquid / informationally-
efficient instrument; informed flow reprices it first, thinner alt books absorb the same
information with a lag. Signal fires long/short on an alt when BTC has ALREADY moved
more than BTC_THRESH_BPS over BTC_LOOKBACK closed bars but the alt itself has NOT yet
caught up (its own trailing return is still within ALT_LAG_CAP_BPS), betting the alt
continues toward BTC's direction as the lag closes. Closed bars only: every return uses
shift(k) with k>0 (backward-looking), never shift(-k) or any forward index use. The BTC
reference series is always loaded at era='train' regardless of caller, so no holdout row
is ever touched by this signal; reindexing onto df.index means a truncated prefix of the
traded symbol's df yields exactly the same historical BTC-derived values as the full
frame (shift is a backward-only, position-local operation), so the whole-prefix causality
check passes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from research.swarm.lib import load_data as ld

DATASET = "long_1h"
TIMEFRAME = "1h"
BTC_LOOKBACK = 3
BTC_THRESH_BPS = 150.0
ALT_LAG_CAP_BPS = 60.0


def signals(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    btc = ld.load_ohlcv("BTC", TIMEFRAME, era="train", dataset=DATASET)
    btc_ret_bps = (btc["close"] / btc["close"].shift(BTC_LOOKBACK) - 1.0) * 1e4
    btc_ret_bps = btc_ret_bps.reindex(df.index)

    alt_ret_bps = (df["close"] / df["close"].shift(BTC_LOOKBACK) - 1.0) * 1e4

    long_sig = (btc_ret_bps > BTC_THRESH_BPS) & (alt_ret_bps < ALT_LAG_CAP_BPS)
    short_sig = (btc_ret_bps < -BTC_THRESH_BPS) & (alt_ret_bps > -ALT_LAG_CAP_BPS)

    out = pd.Series(0, index=df.index, dtype=int)
    out[long_sig.fillna(False)] = 1
    out[short_sig.fillna(False)] = -1
    return out
